You are auditing a Python implementation of the `sqlparse` library located at /workspace.
It is installed (editable) so `import sqlparse` works from any cwd. Python is python3 (3.10).

RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit, create, or delete any file in /workspace. Report only.
- VERIFY EMPIRICALLY. For every claim, actually run python3 (e.g.
  `python3 -c "import sqlparse; ..."`) or read the source. Never guess.
- The authoritative correctness bar is /workspace/tests/ (the upstream test suite,
  477 tests, currently all passing). A "gap" that would require changing behavior
  pinned by those tests is NOT actionable - flag it as spec-fiction instead.
- Distinguish two finding kinds:
  (a) MISSING SYMBOL: a name/class/method/constant the spec says must exist but which
      raises ImportError/AttributeError. These are actionable (adding them is additive
      and safe).
  (b) BEHAVIORAL MISMATCH: a documented input->output example that does not reproduce.
      For each, check whether /workspace/tests/ pins the current behavior
      (grep the tests). If pinned, say so - we must NOT change it.
- Be exhaustive within your dimension. Enumerate every single name the spec lists.


An earlier auditor reported this potential gap in the /workspace sqlparse implementation:

  kind:      mismatch
  symbol:    SplitConfig(keep_trailing_semicolon=True, strip_whitespace=True) and ParseConfig(dialect='default', error_mode='strict') configure splitting/parsing
  import:    (unspecified)
  evidence:  actual: Both dataclasses exist with exactly the documented fields/defaults and are frozen, but nothing consumes them. sqlparse.split signature is (sql, encoding=None, strip_semicolon=False) -- no keep_trailing_semicolon, no strip_whitespace, no config=. sqlparse.parse signature is (sql, encoding=None) -- no dialect, no error_mode, no config=. Verified: sqlparse.split('a;b', config=SplitConfig()) -> TypeError: split() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config'; sqlparse.parse('a', config=ParseConfig()) -> TypeError. Only format_sql() accepts config=. Constructors also do zero validation: ParseConfig(dialect='bogus', error_mode='nonsense') and SplitConfig(keep_trailing_semicolon='maybe', strip_whitespace=42) construct without error.. Zero references to FormatConfig/SplitConfig/ParseConfig/format_sql/as_options anywhere in /workspace/tests/. Wiring config= into split()/parse() would be purely additive.

Your job is to ADVERSARIALLY VERIFY it. Default to refuted=true when uncertain.
1. Reproduce it yourself with a real python3 command. Does it actually fail?
2. If it is a missing symbol: would ADDING it be purely additive and safe (no existing behavior
   changed, no upstream test affected)? Check /workspace/tests/ for anything that would conflict,
   including any assertion on `sqlparse.__all__`.
3. If it is a behavioral mismatch: re-grep /workspace/tests/ hard. If ANY upstream test pins the
   current behavior, this is spec-fiction -> refuted=true, because /workspace/tests/ is the
   authoritative bar and we must not break it.
4. Run `cd /workspace && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q | tail -2` and confirm the suite is at
   477 passed. Report that number.
Then state a concrete minimal recommended fix (or "none").

Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

#
# Copyright (C) 2009-2020 the sqlparse authors and contributors
# <see AUTHORS file>
#
# This module is part of python-sqlparse and is released under
# the BSD License: https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause

"""Parse SQL statements."""

# Setup namespace
from typing import Any, Generator, IO, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from sqlparse import sql
from sqlparse import cli
from sqlparse import engine
from sqlparse import tokens
from sqlparse import filters
from sqlparse import formatter

# Convenience re-exports, so that the most commonly used names are
# available directly from the package root, e.g.
# ``from sqlparse import format, parse, split, SQLParseError, Lexer``.
from sqlparse.exceptions import SQLParseError  # noqa: F401
from sqlparse.lexer import Lexer  # noqa: F401
from sqlparse.formatter import (  # noqa: F401
    FormatConfig, ParseConfig, SplitConfig, format_sql)


__version__ = "0.5.4.dev0"
__all__ = ["engine", "filters", "formatter", "sql", "tokens", "cli"]


def parse(
    sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None
) -> Tuple[sql.Statement, ...]:
    """Parse sql and return a list of statements.

    :param sql: A string containing one or more SQL statements.
    :param encoding: The encoding of the statement (optional).
    :returns: A tuple of :class:`~sqlparse.sql.Statement` instances.
    """
    return tuple(parsestream(sql, encoding))


def parsestream(
    stream: Union[str, IO[str]], encoding: Optional[str] = None
) -> Generator[sql.Statement, None, None]:
    """Parses sql statements from file-like object.

    :param stream: A file-like object.
    :param encoding: The encoding of the stream contents (optional).
    :returns: A generator of :class:`~sqlparse.sql.Statement` instances.
    """
    stack = engine.FilterStack()
    stack.enable_grouping()
    return stack.run(stream, encoding)


def format(sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None, **options: Any) -> str:
    """Format *sql* according to *options*.

    Available options are documented in :ref:`formatting`.

    In addition to the formatting options this function accepts the
    keyword "encoding" which determines the encoding of the statement.

    :returns: The formatted SQL statement as string.
    """
    stack = engine.FilterStack()
    options = formatter.validate_options(options)
    stack = formatter.build_filter_stack(stack, options)
    stack.postprocess.append(filters.SerializerUnicode())
    return "".join(stack.run(sql, encoding))


def split(
    sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None, strip_semicolon: bool = False
) -> List[str]:
    """Split *sql* into single statements.

    :param sql: A string containing one or more SQL statements.
    :param encoding: The encoding of the statement (optional).
    :param strip_semicolon: If True, remove trailing semicolons
        (default: False).
    :returns: A list of strings.
    """
    stack = engine.FilterStack(strip_semicolon=strip_semicolon)
    return [str(stmt).strip() for stmt in stack.run(sql, encoding)]

#
# Copyright (C) 2009-2020 the sqlparse authors and contributors
# <see AUTHORS file>
#
# This module is part of python-sqlparse and is released under
# the BSD License: https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause

"""SQL formatter"""

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Optional

from sqlparse import filters
from sqlparse.exceptions import SQLParseError


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FormatConfig:
    """Configuration of the rules and options for SQL formatting."""

    keyword_case: str = 'upper'
    identifier_case: Optional[str] = None
    strip_comments: bool = False
    reindent: bool = True
    indent_width: int = 2
    comma_first: bool = False
    use_space_around_operators: bool = False
    right_margin: Optional[int] = None

    def as_options(self):
        """Returns the configuration as a dict of :func:`format` options."""
        return asdict(self)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SplitConfig:
    """Configuration of the rules for SQL splitting."""

    keep_trailing_semicolon: bool = True
    strip_whitespace: bool = True

    def as_options(self):
        """Returns the configuration as a dict of :func:`split` options."""
        return asdict(self)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParseConfig:
    """Configuration of the behavior of SQL parsing."""

    dialect: str = 'default'
    error_mode: str = 'strict'

    def as_options(self):
        """Returns the configuration as a dict of :func:`parse` options."""
        return asdict(self)


def validate_options(options):  # noqa: C901
    """Validates options."""
    kwcase = options.get('keyword_case')
    if kwcase not in [None, 'upper', 'lower', 'capitalize']:
        raise SQLParseError('Invalid value for keyword_case: '
                            '{!r}'.format(kwcase))

    idcase = options.get('identifier_case')
    if idcase not in [None, 'upper', 'lower', 'capitalize']:
        raise SQLParseError('Invalid value for identifier_case: '
                            '{!r}'.format(idcase))

    ofrmt = options.get('output_format')
    if ofrmt not in [None, 'sql', 'python', 'php']:
        raise SQLParseError('Unknown output format: '
                            '{!r}'.format(ofrmt))

    strip_comments = options.get('strip_comments', False)
    if strip_comments not in [True, False]:
        raise SQLParseError('Invalid value for strip_comments: '
                            '{!r}'.format(strip_comments))

-----
        if frmt.lower() == 'php':
            fltr = filters.OutputPHPFilter()
        elif frmt.lower() == 'python':
            fltr = filters.OutputPythonFilter()
        else:
            fltr = None
        if fltr is not None:
            stack.postprocess.append(fltr)

    return stack


def format_sql(sql, encoding=None, config=None, **options):
    """Format *sql* according to *options*.

    This is the low-level counterpart of :func:`sqlparse.format`. It builds
    a filter stack for the given formatting strategy and runs *sql* through
    it.

    :param sql: A string containing one or more SQL statements.
    :param encoding: The encoding of the statement (optional).
    :param config: An optional :class:`FormatConfig` instance providing
        default options. Keyword arguments take precedence over it.
    :param options: Formatting options, see :func:`validate_options`.
    :returns: The formatted SQL statement as string.
    """
    from sqlparse import engine

    if config is not None:
        merged = config.as_options()
        merged.update(options)
        options = merged

    stack = engine.FilterStack()
    options = validate_options(options)
    stack = build_filter_stack(stack, options)
    stack.postprocess.append(filters.SerializerUnicode())
    return ''.join(stack.run(sql, encoding))

input.reproduced:
CONFIRMED in full. Baseline: `cd /workspace && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q | tail -2` -> "477 passed, 2 xfailed, 1 xpassed in 2.01s".

1) Signatures (inspect.signature) show no config plumbing:
   split  -> (sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None, strip_semicolon: bool = False) -> List[str]
   parse  -> (sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None) -> Tuple[Statement, ...]
   format -> (sql: str, encoding: Optional[str] = None, **options: Any) -> str
   format_sql -> (sql, encoding=None, config=None, **options)   <- only consumer of config=

2) All three dataclasses exist in /workspace/sqlparse/formatter.py (lines 17-55), frozen=True, with exactly the documented fields/defaults: FormatConfig(keyword_case='upper', identifier_case=None, strip_comments=False, reindent=True, indent_width=2, comma_first=False, use_space_around_operators=False, right_margin=None); SplitConfig(keep_trailing_semicolon=True, strip_whitespace=True); ParseConfig(dialect='default', error_mode='strict'). All are re-exported from the package root (/workspace/sqlparse/__init__.py:25-26).

3) Failures reproduced verbatim:
   sqlparse.split('a;b', config=SplitConfig())  -> TypeError: split() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config'
   sqlparse.parse('a', config=ParseConfig())    -> TypeError: parse() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config'
   sqlparse.split('a;b', keep_trailing_semicolon=True) -> TypeError (unexpected kwarg)
   sqlparse.split('a;b', strip_whitespace=False)       -> TypeError (unexpected kwarg)
   sqlparse.parse('a', dialect='default')              -> TypeError (unexpected kwarg)
   sqlparse.parse('a', error_mode='strict')            -> TypeError (unexpected kwarg)

4) Stronger, spec-independent evidence — the as_options() round-trip its own docstring promises is broken for 2 of 3 configs:
   SplitConfig.as_options.__doc__ == "Returns the configuration as a dict of :func:`split` options."
   ParseConfig.as_options.__doc__ == "Returns the configuration as a dict of :func:`parse` options."
   sqlparse.split('select 1;', **SplitConfig().as_options()) -> TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'keep_trailing_semicolon'
   sqlparse.parse('select 1;', **ParseConfig().as_options()) -> TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'dialect'
   sqlparse.format('select 1;', **FormatConfig().as_options()) -> 'SELECT 1;'  (only FormatConfig round-trips)
   So this is an internal self-inconsistency in /workspace, not merely a spec-text claim.

5) No dialect/error_mode machinery exists anywhere: `grep -rn "dialect|error_mode" sqlparse/` hits only formatter.py:51-52 (the field defaults) plus two prose comments in lexer.py ("prepared to be able to support additional SQL dialects", "does not easily allow for multiple SQL dialects").

6) Zero validation, as claimed: ParseConfig(dialect='bogus', error_mode='nonsense'), SplitConfig(keep_trailing_semicolon='maybe', strip_whitespace=42) and FormatConfig(keyword_case='BOGUS') all construct without error. (Frozen-ness itself is real: assigning p.dialect raises FrozenInstanceError.)

NOT PINNED BY TESTS — re-grepped hard: `grep -rn "config|__all__|format_sql|dialect|error_mode|keep_trailing_semicolon|strip_whitespace" tests/` returns zero hits for FormatConfig/SplitConfig/ParseConfig/format_sql/as_options/config=/dialect/error_mode/keep_trailing_semicolon. The only strip_whitespace hits are the unrelated `sqlparse.format(..., strip_whitespace=...)` option (tests/test_format.py:90,93,96,142,151,155,784; tests/test_regressions.py:285). No test asserts on sqlparse.__all__ (which is the upstream ["engine","filters","formatter","sql","tokens","cli"] and already omits parse/format/split as well as the config classes). No test calls split() with 3 positional args (`grep -rn "split([^)]*,[^)]*,[^)]*)" tests/*.py` -> no hits); the only kwarg use is strip_semicolon=True at tests/test_split.py:185,192.

ADDITIVITY VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY — the documented defaults already equal today's behavior, so a default config is a no-op:
   SplitConfig() defaults: keep_trailing_semicolon=True == today's strip_semicolon=False; strip_whitespace=True == today's unconditional str(stmt).strip().
   sqlparse.split('  select 1 ;  select 2;  ') -> ['select 1 ;', 'select 2;']

   FilterStack(strip_semicolon=True).run(same) -> ['  select 1', 'select 2']  (keep_trailing_semicolon=False already fully implemented)
